You are the writer of the discussion described below. You write out the discussion that the participants listed below take part in, under the rules and the flow given.

## Setting
Selection of a service expansion proposal for a public library system. Five reviewers drawn from library staff and the community board deliberate over proposals for expanding services. One proposal will be implemented across the branch network. Participants: Benjamin, Shizue, Rin, Jonathan and Minako. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.
Things that can be looked into (titles only):
- Running and equipment lines last year
- County grant terms and the endowment
- Quoted delivery windows from suppliers
- Winter road closures north of the river
- Attendance sheets from former outreach stops
- Two programmes begun six years ago
- Bus links in the two outer wards
- Evening room bookings and remote catalogue use
- Volunteer register and supervision training
- Neighbourhood associations and tool certification

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Shizue, Jonathan, Rin, Benjamin and Minako. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the candidates | 4 turns | every participant votes; the candidate with the most votes is selected |
- Several participants may choose the same thing; what is found out is told only to the participant who looked into it.
If votes are tied, one of the tied candidates is chosen by a fixed rule. The discussion ends after the vote.

## Looking into things
After round 1, each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into. What they find out is told only to that participant.

## Participants
Name: Benjamin
Age: 28
Gender: male
Personality: Benjamin is an intelligent and calm person. He is able to think calmly and rationally, and even in emotional situations, he places importance on logic. In public, he is elegant and polite, often incorporating sarcasm and humor into his conversations, but he is skilled at doing so without hurting others, creating a harmonious atmosphere. He also has an introverted side, often engrossed in deep thought, and occasionally keeps his distance from those around him. However, his calmness and knowledge are factors that earn him the trust of others even in difficult situations.
Concern: Every budget cycle looks sufficient on the day of the vote and thin by the second year, and the trouble seems to lie in how the funding is shaped rather than in its size.

Name: Shizue
Age: 78
Gender: female
Personality: Shizue has a very calm and gentle personality. Even as she has grown older, she continues to smile warmly at those around her and is a very caring person. She is always considerate of others, friendly, and sometimes shows a playful side. She often reaches out to those who are feeling down with kind words and never hesitates to lend a helping hand when needed, which has earned her the affection of many people in the village and community. Through her years of life experience, Shizue has come to understand the importance of living peacefully with others.
Concern: Too much of what we have started here depended on conditions we do not control, and the last few timetables came apart in the months when those conditions turned against us.

Name: Rin
Age: 9
Gender: female
Personality: Rin is an active and energetic girl. She can be a little precocious at times, and when she is with her older brothers and sisters, she makes mature comments and comes up with interesting ideas. She is very curious and loves adventure and trying new things. She can be a little clumsy at times, often surprising and amusing those around her, but her cheerful personality makes her loved by everyone.
Concern: It bothers me that we keep judging new ideas by how they sound in the room, when shapes very like them have already been tried in this system and left records nobody reopens.

Name: Jonathan
Age: 38
Gender: male
Personality: Jonathan has a calm and introverted personality and values inner peace. He prefers spending quiet time alone rather than forming deep connections with others. As a result, he loves books and knowledge and reads frequently. When interacting with others, he is gentle and kind, occasionally flashing an unexpected smile. Though he exudes a mysterious and serene aura, he rarely shares personal details about himself with others. Those around him often find comfort in his quiet kindness and composed demeanor.
Concern: What keeps nagging at me is the knock-on: where our buildings sit and when they open already decides who can reach us, and every new commitment quietly reshuffles that.

Name: Minako
Age: 28
Gender: female
Personality: Minako is very calm and acts calmly in any situation. Even when those around her are emotional, she grasps the facts firmly and responds calmly. As a result, she is often asked for her opinion and often takes on a leadership role. She rarely shows her emotions, but she also has a kind side that she shows to those she trusts. She can be a little stubborn and is strong in her convictions. She is also confident in her physical strength and never neglects her training.
Concern: Staff absorb every new commitment on top of what they already do, and nobody checks beforehand whether the skills it needs are actually sitting on the roster.

## Hidden information
The candidates and the full text of every card are listed here. The participants do not know them before the schedule above says so, and nothing from them may appear in the talk before the round in which it is revealed.

Candidates (see the schedule above):
- A: Mobile Branch Service. A vehicle-based lending service that visits outlying neighborhoods on a fixed weekly schedule, carrying a rotating collection and a staffed help desk at each stop.
- B: Maker Workshop. A dedicated room in the main branch offering tools, materials, and scheduled instruction sessions for residents working on craft, repair, and electronics projects.
- C: Language Learning Circles. A recurring program of conversation groups and tutoring sessions in several languages, coordinated with trained facilitators and partner community organizations across the district.
- D: Digital Archive Portal. A program to scan local newspapers, photographs, and municipal records and publish them through a searchable portal with browsing and citation tools for researchers.

Cards (see the schedule above; title: text):
- Running and equipment lines last year: Last year's ledger shows the vehicle running line overran by a third, while the one-off equipment allocation closed under budget and was handed back to reserves.
- County grant terms and the endowment: The county grant pays contracted session fees for twelve months only, after which the flat operating budget carries them; capital items draw on the endowment instead.
- Quoted delivery windows from suppliers: Both regional scanning contractors quoted last spring attach delivery windows that slip whenever a larger municipal client books first; bench tooling ships from stock within weeks.
- Winter road closures north of the river: Access roads north of the river were shut on eleven days last winter, yet the community halls in those wards kept their own evening timetables without interruption.
- Attendance sheets from former outreach stops: Attendance sheets from the outreach stops run until that funding lapsed averaged forty visitors a session in the outer wards, above anything the main building drew midweek.
- Two programmes begun six years ago: A photographic digitisation batch attempted six years ago left half its images unindexed, while the partner-run evening groups begun that same season still meet unaided.
- Bus links in the two outer wards: Two outer wards lost their bus link when the county rerouted services, and residents there now face an hour's round trip to reach any staffed counter.
- Evening room bookings and remote catalogue use: Evening room bookings are full through the term and caretakers lock up at nine, though remote catalogue use from home peaks well after that hour.
- Volunteer register and supervision training: The volunteer register lists a dozen retired tradespeople already running the Saturday repair clinic, but no one on the payroll is trained to supervise outside facilitators.
- Neighbourhood associations and tool certification: Two neighbourhood associations staff their own weekly sessions with people they prepared themselves, while the technician who kept the power tools certified retired in spring.
